geo.label: on hold / consumer softening
parts: Macro Stance

The consumer is cooling: December retail sales stalled, with Reuters flagging underlying weakness [[n7071]]. The Fed is not reacting yet; Cleveland's Hammack says rates could be on hold 'for quite some time' [[n7698]]. Softer demand plus a patient Fed argues for lower front-end yields and a weaker dollar, not a growth scare in equities, unless payrolls crack.
Rates & Curve

The 2Y closed at 3.45% and the 10Y at 4.16%, a 10Y−2Y spread of 71 bps; over 20 observations the 2Y fell 9 bps and the 10Y 3 bps, and over five observations both fell 12 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-10). The curve is moderately steep, approaching the long-run average, and the 20-observation move is a bull steepening (both down, 2Y down more). The S&P 500 closed at 6,941.81, down 0.33%, with the VIX at 17.79 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).
New / Most Important

The delayed January jobs report is released Wednesday, with inflation data also on this week's slate [[n7055]] [[n7544]]. The White House is already seeking to downplay any slowdown [[n7056]]. Under the surface, Wall Street's anything-but-tech trade is reshaping the market: the Dow closed at 50,188.14 while the Nasdaq 100 is down 2.56% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10) [[n7757]].
Playbook ✓

Own 2Y Treasuries and the bull steepener into payrolls; keep equity exposure in industrials, energy and materials rather than mega-cap tech or discretionary. Change the call if payrolls surprise strongly and the 2Y retraces above 3.54%, its level 20 observations ago (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-10).

geo.label: on hold / easing bias
parts: Macro Stance

The ECB kept rates steady and shrugged off the inflation dip, but its own research now argues that foreign import tariffs mean lower inflation and weaker activity for the euro area [[n2666]] [[n7796]]. With inflation at 1.7% in January, the next move is more likely a cut than a hike [[n2620]].
Activity & Inflation

EUR/USD closed at 1.1904, up 0.66% in the prior session and 2.03% over 20 sessions, an extra disinflationary force (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). The STOXX 600 closed at 620.97, up 1.72% over 20 sessions, while the DAX is down 1.7% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).
New / Most Important

Company results are carrying Europe: Philips surged 12% on a clear step-up in sales even as European stocks closed down, Kering jumped 12% as its new CEO mapped a revival, and Barclays beat and plans to return £15bn to investors [[n2898]] [[n2401]] [[n2460]]. Turnaround stories with capital returns are being paid.
Playbook ✓

Overweight European banks, insurers and quality cyclicals with self-help stories; fund from US mega-cap tech. Add Bund duration on back-ups. Avoid German autos and exporters most exposed to a strong euro. Change the call if EUR/USD gains force a growth downgrade or if AI-disruption selling spreads further into European financials.

geo.label: easing support / weak demand
parts: Macro Stance

Policy is leaning toward support while demand stays weak. The PBOC promised financial support to boost domestic demand, and Beijing is tightening market oversight to engineer a 'slow bull' in equities [[n0917]] [[n0978]]. Real activity has not turned, so we stay Mixed: own policy-backed equities and the currency, avoid consumption-exposed cyclicals.
PMIs & Activity

The latest official manufacturing PMI, for January, dropped to 49.3, in contraction [[n0540]]. The new hard data point is worse: China's auto sales fell at the fastest pace in nearly two years in January [[n7083]]. Confirmation of a turn would need the February official PMI back above 50 and a stabilisation in car sales once trade-in subsidies kick in.
Credit Impulse

The feed carries no January credit or aggregate financing print yet. The signal is policy intent: the PBOC's pledge of financial support for domestic demand points to targeted relending rather than broad rate cuts [[n0917]]. Regulators are also urging banks to curb exposure to US Treasuries, which keeps more liquidity onshore [[n7547]]. We treat the impulse as modestly positive pending the data.
Property

The Shenzhen government is drafting an $11.6 billion rescue package for China Vanke, according to Octus [[n0957]]. That is the clearest sign yet that local governments will backstop large developers rather than let them fail, but S&P still expects the property slump to be worse than it previously forecast this year [[n0859]]. Credit risk is falling faster than sales are recovering, so prefer developer bonds over equity, and watch whether other cities copy Shenzhen.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

China plans to invest 5 trillion yuan in its power grid over the next 5 years, a direct support for grid equipment, cables and copper demand [[n0921]]. Fiscal policy otherwise stays targeted rather than broad, favouring infrastructure over household transfers. On trade, Europe is debating a 'mega tariff': a French minister urged caution amid calls for a 30% duty on Chinese goods [[n0961]]. That keeps Chinese exporters' European growth at risk just as US access narrows.
Markets & Flows

The Hang Seng closed at 27,183.15, up 1.25% over 20 sessions, and the Shanghai Composite at 4,128.37, down 0.25% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). ASHR closed at 34.03 and KWEB at 34.31, down 8.9% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). USD/CNY closed at 6.9220, down 0.24% in the prior session and 0.73% over 20 sessions, extending the yuan's run (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). Chinese stocks won the most MSCI index additions in nearly three years [[n0979]].
New / Most Important

The MSCI additions and the 'slow bull' oversight push matter most for flows: passive money is being pulled into A-shares just as regulators try to dampen volatility [[n0979]] [[n0978]]. The Vanke rescue reduces tail risk in the property chain [[n0957]].
Playbook ✓

Own CNY strength and A-share index exposure via ASHR, plus grid-equipment and copper beneficiaries of the 5 trillion yuan plan [[n0921]]; avoid Hong Kong internet, with KWEB down 8.9% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10), and auto makers. Change the call if the January credit data disappoint or the yuan reverses. ⚠ Divergence: Beijing is adding support and index inclusion is pulling in money, yet auto sales just fell at the fastest pace in nearly two years [[n7083]]; the equity bid is running ahead of the real economy.

earnings_pattern.title: Turnarounds and capital returns are paid; consumer misses are not
parts: Rewarded

Self-help and capital returns: Kering jumped 12% as its new CEO mapped a revival, Philips surged 12% on a step-up in sales, Barclays plans to return £15bn, and Spotify jumped on subscriber growth [[n2401]] [[n2898]] [[n2460]] [[n2423]]. CBA's record half lifted its shares [[n0262]].
Punished

Consumer and AI-exposed misses: Ford posted its worst miss in four years, Coca-Cola forecast only modest growth, CVS fell despite a beat, and Robinhood's revenue disappointed on a crypto slowdown [[n2419]] [[n2431]] [[n2397]] [[n7785]]. CSL plunged to an eight-year low [[n2434]].
Pattern

The market pays for internal catalysts it can underwrite — a new CEO, a cost plan, a buyback — and punishes anything that depends on the consumer or on crypto volumes. Beats without raised guidance are sold.
Attention into EPS
Cisco and McDonald's report alongside the delayed jobs and inflation data [[n7544]]. Coinbase also has earnings this week, after JPMorgan cut its price target to $290 [[n2351]] [[n1467]].
Playbook

Own self-help stories in Europe and financials with capital-return plans; avoid consumer-exposed names into the remaining prints. Fade post-earnings bounces in crypto-linked brokers. The pattern breaks if payrolls are strong enough to revive consumer names.

anticipatory.title: CJEU WIBOR ruling and Polish banks
parts: What Is Priced

The EU Court of Justice rules on WIBOR on 12 February, and Bankier asks whether it will be a breakthrough for borrowers [[n4568]]. PKO BP is down 4.08% over five sessions and closed at 92.56, while Pekao is still up 9.67% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).
Conditional Expression

Borrower-friendly ruling: sell PKO BP and Pekao, buy insurers such as PZU and Orlen as relative havens. Bank-friendly ruling: buy the banks back, since the five-session drawdown would reverse quickly.
Risk

A split or ambiguous ruling could leave the legal risk open for months, which is worse for valuations than a clear outcome. After the five-session pullback in PKO BP, a benign ruling could produce a sharp relief move.

catalysts.title: $COIN — crypto drought into the print
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Coinbase reports this week, and JPMorgan cut its price target to $290 ahead of earnings [[n2351]] [[n1467]]. Robinhood's revenue just disappointed on a crypto slowdown, a direct read-across to Coinbase's transaction revenue [[n7785]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

COIN closed at 162.51, down 2.83% in the prior session and 33.12% over 20 sessions, a steeper fall than bitcoin's 23.03% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). A close back above 242.98, its level 20 sessions ago, is far away; the near-term trigger to cover is a guide that shows stabilising retail volumes. Risk: renewed ETF inflows and a bitcoin bounce could spark a short squeeze after the print.

catalysts.title: $TSM — record capex approval
parts: Catalyst & Thesis
TSMC's board approved a record $45 billion spending package on new fabs [[n6010]]. The approval confirms customer demand visibility for advanced nodes and AI packaging.
Price Hurdle & Risk

TSM closed at 361.91, up 7.79% over five sessions and 9.08% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). Add on pullbacks toward 331.77, its level 20 sessions ago, rather than chasing (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). Risk: higher capex weighs on free cash flow if AI demand cools, and US pressure to relocate capacity adds cost.

catalysts.title: $MCD — low-income consumer squeeze
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

McDonald's reports this week [[n7544]]. The FT asks what fast food's downturn says about the US economy, and December retail sales stalled [[n2865]] [[n7071]]. McDonald's core low-income customer is the most exposed to that slowdown.
Price Hurdle & Risk

MCD is not on our market card; the sector context is XLY down 4.97% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). The thesis breaks if US comparable sales show value menus winning share from pricier chains; in that case cover and rotate into the value winners.

retail.title: Robinhood / HOOD — prediction markets vs. crypto drought
parts: Observed Attention
The WSJ says Robinhood got a prediction-market lift despite its cooling crypto business, while Reuters reports its revenue disappointed and shares fell [[n4735]] [[n7785]].
Motivation & Bias
Retail treats HOOD as a proxy for its own trading activity; the new prediction-market line feeds a narrative bias that new products can offset falling crypto volumes.
Instrument & Risk

Prefer defined-risk options over shares into the next print, and size small: HOOD is a high-beta proxy for retail activity that has been falling alongside COIN, down 33.12% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). Risk: crypto volumes keep falling, and prediction-market revenue is too small to offset them.

retail.title: Bitcoin / IBIT — retail capitulation abroad
parts: Observed Attention
Bloomberg reports South Koreans bailing on crypto as retail traders bemoan losses [[n1456]]. IBIT closed at 38.97, down 24.87% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).
Motivation & Bias

Loss aversion is turning into capitulation, often a late-cycle signal. US ETF buyers are doing the opposite, with back-to-back inflows, which suggests institutions are absorbing retail selling [[n1428]].
Instrument & Risk
Accumulate through spot ETFs in small increments; avoid leveraged products. Risk: bitcoin's 23.03% fall over 20 sessions could extend if ETF inflows fade (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).

retail.title: Gold and silver / GLD, SLV — 'all greed, no fear'
parts: Observed Attention
Bloomberg says it's all greed and no fear in India's gold and silver markets [[n4734]]. SLV fell 3.46% in the prior session to 73.41 and GLD 0.99% to 462.40 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10).
Motivation & Bias
Retail is chasing a momentum trade in precious metals; FOMO is strongest where volatility has been highest.
Instrument & Risk

Prefer GLD over SLV; silver is down 5.19% over 20 sessions while gold is up 9.02%, so silver's swings punish late buyers (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). Risk: margin hikes and forced liquidations.

retail.title: Hims & Hers / HIMS — the GLP-1 trade gets real
parts: Observed Attention
Stocktwits lists HIMS among the names on traders' radar, and Seeking Alpha downgraded it as 'the GLP-1 trade just got real' [[n2353]] [[n4738]].
Motivation & Bias
Retail is drawn by the obesity-drug narrative and the stock's volatility; confirmation bias keeps the story alive even as the competitive landscape changes.
Instrument & Risk

HIMS is not on our card; trade it only with defined-risk options and small size. Risk: competition from branded GLP-1 makers such as Lilly, which closed at 1,025.00 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10), and regulatory scrutiny of compounded drugs.
